message:
test(host): what a window that will never answer costs in total

Test 1. No product change.

Both halves were checked alone: the budget stops asking after three failures, and the helper path
gives up at the deadline. Neither of those is the property the session needs. That property is
arithmetic over the two -- a window that will never answer has to cost a bounded amount ACROSS
requests, not a deadline on each one forever.

Twelve requests against a helper that never answers: three reach it, nine are answered without
touching a helper at all, and the sequence costs 1222ms across three runs instead of the 4800ms
twelve deadlines would be. The lower bound is checked too, so a budget that refused everything
from the start would fail this rather than look like a win.

What this is not: the control session. That composes the same two pieces inside a lambda that
needs a live link, and running it needs a client. This drives them in the same order against the
same stalling helper, which makes it the arithmetic the session depends on and not the session
itself. The remaining gap is unchanged -- a real host, a real picker, and a measurement showing
the control channel answering other requests while one window is timing out.

19 checks, three runs clean.
